sections.heading: State And Local Tax Accounts
paragraphs: Keep the legal entity name, federal identification number, location addresses and each tax account in an account register. Alabama's sales/use division administers several different programs, including consumer use, seller use, rental and lodging taxes. Choose accounts from the actual business activity rather than treating the sales tax registration as permission to ignore other obligations.

ONE SPOT through My Alabama Taxes supports state and local filing, including local taxes administered outside the state department. Preserve the locality and tax type on each confirmation. A single portal does not mean a city assessment can be offset against a state sales tax balance without authorization.

sections.heading: Sales And Purchase Evidence
paragraphs: Alabama's record statute calls for suitable gross sales and receipts records, purchase invoices and books that permit the department to determine liability. Maintain item descriptions, gross transaction amounts, delivery information, tax charged and documentary support for exempt treatment. Marketplace reports should remain distinguishable from direct sales.

For payables, retain the vendor invoice, delivery location, purchase purpose and payment. Identify bills with no tax line for consumer use tax review. A supplier's omission does not settle the buyer's obligation. Do not assign a rate or exemption merely from a postal city name; local jurisdiction and the transaction facts need review.

sections.heading: Withholding And Unemployment
paragraphs: The current department forms list separate monthly, quarterly and annual withholding forms, including the A3 annual reconciliation. Maintain employee certificates, payroll registers, payment acknowledgments and the actual reporting schedule assigned to the employer. Reconcile withheld tax separately from gross wage expense and net pay.

Unemployment reporting belongs to the labor agency rather than the income tax withholding account. Keep the unemployment account, assigned rate notices, wage reports and benefit correspondence distinct. The official new hire resource refers to the federal employer number used for quarterly reporting. Worker status, mobile workers and possible local occupational tax require a payroll professional's review.

sections.heading: Receipts, Bills And Monthly Reporting
paragraphs: As a general bookkeeping routine, separate customer payments from loans and owner funding, match vendor payments to approved invoices and reconcile bank and card accounts. Investigate unmatched transfers before producing the balance sheet. A bank statement explains cash movement but not whether a sale was taxable or a worker was correctly classified.

Prepare an independent roll forward for each state/local tax liability and withholding account. Show opening balance, activity, payments and unresolved differences. When one electronic withdrawal pays several jurisdictions, preserve the allocation rather than posting the entire payment against whichever tax account is easiest to find.

sections.heading: Illustration: A Retailer With Two Locations
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: an Alabama retailer has two stores and receives one processor settlement for both. The bookkeeper preserves store level gross sales, returns, certificate support and settlement fees. The preparer can then evaluate the correct local treatment instead of treating the combined deposit as one location's sales.

The retailer also buys a display fixture without a tax line. Record its invoice and intended use separately from inventory for resale, then request a consumer use tax determination. This example supplies no tax rate or automatic registration conclusion.

sections.heading: Business Privilege And Corporate Income Records
paragraphs: Alabama business privilege tax and corporate income tax are different obligations. Revenue explains that privilege tax can apply to corporations, limited liability entities and disregarded entities, including businesses registered in Alabama even when inactive, subject to the current small tax exemption. Corporate income tax concerns corporate taxable income attributable to Alabama. Keep federal classification elections, formation or withdrawal documents and prior returns so the preparer can determine which filings and exemptions apply.

For bookkeeping, preserve annual balance sheet support, ownership changes, Alabama receipts and receipts elsewhere, and the federal return with state adjustment workpapers. Maintain privilege tax and corporate income payments in separate schedules from payroll and sales taxes. At each monthly close, match estimates and credits to the correct tax year and record only a supported provision approved by the preparer. The annual handoff should include exemption calculations, payment confirmations and any dissolution correspondence; an idle bank account does not prove the entity has completed its obligations.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Workforce Alabama requires employers in its unemployment system to file a contribution and wage report for each quarter online; an annual combined report is not a substitute. Its FAQ provides a correction process and access to prior reports. Preserve employee quarterly wages, the assigned rate notice, accepted report and payment evidence. Reconcile employer contribution expense and the unpaid contribution balance separately from employee income tax withholding. Give the preparer the four quarterly reports and corrections at year end so wages can be compared with payroll totals without erasing the original quarter.

sections.heading: Year End, Retention And Scope
paragraphs: For year end, organize reconciliations, inventory support, assets, tax filings, payroll totals and unresolved notices for the CPA or enrolled agent. Preserve ownership and business changes so the adviser can assess entity filing requirements. Rental, lodging and other specialized activities require their own review rather than copying a retailer's settings.

Alabama Rule 810-3-70-.02 requires withholding records for three years from the return due date or three years from actual filing, whichever is later. Electronic records must meet the separate electronic recordkeeping rule. This verified payroll category does not establish one destruction date for sales/use, assets, federal records or open disputes. Maintain retrievable source detail and confirm longer holds before deletion.

sections.heading: Local Jurisdiction Records
paragraphs: Alaska's Office of the State Assessor says the state does not levy sales tax, while some cities and boroughs do. Municipalities set their particular rules and forms, and both city and borough taxes can apply. Keep each business location and customer delivery location visible for review rather than labeling every Alaska sale tax free.

Build a jurisdiction register with the relevant municipality, account correspondence, assigned filing information and effective dates of changes. State summaries can describe earlier years; confirm the actual municipal rules before filing. This resource does not determine a remote seller's obligations or substitute one local ordinance for another.

sections.heading: Sales, Exemptions And Purchases
paragraphs: Preserve receipts, item descriptions, service dates, delivery evidence, tax charged, customer refunds and any municipal exemption documents. A settlement deposit cannot demonstrate whether local tax was collected correctly. Local exemptions and caps should be evaluated from the applicable ordinance, not imported from another Alaska community.

For accounts payable, retain invoices and where the purchased item is stored or used. Municipal use tax may exist where sales tax is imposed. If another jurisdiction's tax was paid, preserve that receipt for the adviser to evaluate any credit. Do not create a statewide use tax payable simply because the accounting software offers one.

sections.heading: Employer Accounts And Seasonal Payroll
paragraphs: The Department of Labor and Workforce Development provides a separate unemployment tax account and employer reporting system. Its employer handbook identifies registration, accurate payroll records, quarterly reports, taxes and business change reporting as employer responsibilities. Keep rate notices and confirmations with the wage detail supporting each report.

Seasonal work makes clean payroll history especially useful. Retain hire and separation dates, actual work locations, payment periods, expense reimbursements and the nature of work. Ask a specialist about maritime, fishing, staffing and other special employment arrangements rather than assuming every person paid receives identical treatment.

sections.heading: Revenue, Vendor Bills And Monthly Statements
paragraphs: General accounting practice still applies when no state sales tax exists. Separate operating revenue from financing, owner transfers and deposits for future work. Match supplier bills and credits to payments, reconcile cards and banks, and investigate stale customer balances. Preserve freight and delivery charges with the purchase they support.

Present a consistent income statement and balance sheet, with local tax liabilities separated by municipality and payroll liabilities separated by program. A quiet winter month may still involve unpaid bills or annual expenses. Cash planning should identify those commitments without artificially smoothing real seasonal activity.

sections.heading: Illustration: A Seasonal Equipment Rental
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: an Alaska business rents equipment to customers in more than one municipality. The bookkeeper saves the rental agreement, dates, delivery and return location, deposit, refund and each charge. The local tax preparer can then evaluate the actual jurisdictions and treatment; the example does not assume that all rentals are taxable.

A damaged item is repaired by a vendor and paid with the company card. Keep the repair invoice and connect any customer damage reimbursement to the original rental without hiding either amount inside the net processor deposit. These linked records are useful even where a local tax does not apply.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And Entity Reporting
paragraphs: Alaska has a corporate net income tax program even though it has no individual income tax. Official legislative material identifies the corporate income tax under AS 43.20.011, and Revenue maintains separate corporate and partnership reporting programs. Do not infer from an owner tax return, an LLC name or the absence of a personal state tax that the business has no state filing duty. Ask the preparer to document the entity classification and Alaska activity that determine the actual return.

Keep the federal business return, Alaska operations and receipt detail, ownership interests, asset and payroll locations, and prior state calculations. Reconcile any corporate estimates, return payments and carryforwards by tax year during the monthly close, independently of local sales and employment tax. Include these schedules and federal adjustments in the annual handoff. Corporate group, partnership ownership and specialized industry questions need current return instructions; the corporate forms viewer was not retrievable during this review, so no detailed exemption or filing threshold is asserted.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: The Alaska employer handbook requires quarterly contribution reporting with employee wage detail and explains employee contributions as well as employer tax. Preserve gross wages, hours and employment changes with the quarterly calculation. Reconcile amounts deducted from workers separately from employer expense, then match the combined remittance to the accepted report and bank payment. At year end, compare quarterly wage totals and employee contribution statements with payroll records. Seasonal activity needs accurate quarter allocation rather than shifting all wages into the busiest quarter.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention Decisions
paragraphs: Provide the tax professional with reconciled accounts, equipment purchases and disposals, seasonal payroll reports, local returns, ownership documents and unresolved municipality notices. Review applicable state entity taxes and industry obligations from the actual entity and activity rather than extrapolating from the absence of a statewide sales tax.

Alaska Labor requires accounting and payroll records to be preserved for at least five years. The employer handbook specifies pay periods, wages, hours, wage computation, special payments and employment changes among employee details. Apply that employer requirement separately from municipality sales records and property basis documents. Preserve pending audit and claim evidence and keep readable source detail when changing systems. Local sales retention requires the applicable municipality rule.

sections.heading: TPT Licenses And Business Activity
paragraphs: Arizona describes transaction privilege tax as a tax on the vendor for doing business, rather than an ordinary sales tax on the purchaser. Taxable activities may require licensing, and classification, city and county affect treatment. Keep the legal entity, activity, location and license information together.

A business can have more than one line of work. Preserve contracts and revenue detail that distinguish those activities before the totals reach the tax preparer. The TPT label does not make every receipt taxable, and an income statement category does not automatically establish a statutory business classification.

sections.heading: Sales, Deductions And Purchase Use Tax
paragraphs: Maintain gross receipts before payment processing fees, returns and any proposed deduction. Attach certificates and location evidence to the transaction. ADOR's audit resource identifies income classification, exemptions, deductions and purchase tax among its review areas. Keep the supporting reason for treatment instead of only an exempt flag in software.

For vendor bills, distinguish inventory intended for resale from equipment or supplies consumed by the business. Arizona's TPT resource identifies use tax concerns when goods are used or stored in the state without appropriate tax paid. Send uncertain transactions for a determination, preserving the invoice, payment, use location and any certificate already given.

sections.heading: Payroll And DES Reporting
paragraphs: Arizona DES provides quarterly unemployment tax and wage reporting. Preserve employee identity, gross compensation, work periods, reports, account status changes and payment confirmations. DES warns employers not to simply stop filing when payroll pauses; use the proper account change process and retain its acknowledgment.

Keep income tax withholding obligations and unemployment reporting distinguishable, including separate account evidence and liability reconciliations. A payroll expert should review remote employees, worker status, wage exclusions and benefit deductions. A zero net liability in the general ledger does not establish that required wage detail was filed.

sections.heading: Different Retention Rules
paragraphs: ADOR's business recordkeeping page lists a four year baseline for TPT records from the due date or actual filing, whichever is later, and identifies situations requiring longer preservation. DES separately requires employer records for the most recent four calendar years. ADOR also describes different periods for other records, so do not use one number as an automatic deletion rule.

Retain documentation of exemptions, refunds, asset basis, open audits and unfiled periods according to the applicable requirement. A tax professional should reconcile agency and federal obligations before destruction. Export electronic transaction detail and code definitions before replacing software so the records remain understandable.

sections.heading: Monthly Reporting And Income Evidence
paragraphs: As general bookkeeping practice, distinguish loans and owner deposits from customer revenue, reconcile bank/card accounts and review customer and supplier balances. Preserve invoices supporting receivables and credits reducing payables. Do not net unrelated refunds or transfers against sales to make an account easier to reconcile.

Prepare a TPT workpaper that bridges business revenue to activity and location totals for the preparer. Explain differences from financial statements, including timing, deductions under review and tax reimbursements. Maintain a separate payroll liability roll forward showing what was recorded, paid and remains unresolved.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Entity Classification And Income Tax Support
paragraphs: Arizona treats an LLC electing corporate federal taxation as a corporate income tax filer, while a disregarded single member LLC is included with its owner. Corporate return selection also depends on whether activity is wholly within Arizona or spans states. Retain the actual federal election and business locations. TPT reports describe business activity tax and do not replace income tax records or decide the entity classification.

Maintain federal to state adjustment support, asset schedules and receipts by location for the preparer. Partnership and S corporation owners may have an entity tax election to evaluate; preserve the approved election and owner allocation evidence rather than making it through an unexplained accounting entry. Each month reconcile corporate or elected entity estimates and credits by tax year, separate from employee withholding. At year end include capital changes, owner distributions, prior losses and the final federal return so state adjustments can be reviewed.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Arizona DES distinguishes rated employers paying quarterly tax from eligible reimbursable employers billed for benefit charges. TWS supports wage reports, zero wage reports, operational changes and rate notices. Preserve the account type and contribution calculation so a zero rate on a reimbursable wage report is not mistaken for permission to ignore later bills. Reconcile employer tax or reimbursement expense to the applicable notices and payments each month. Include benefit charges, accepted quarterly files and corrections in the annual payroll handoff; do not simply stop reporting when hiring pauses.

sections.heading: Illustration And Year End Handoff
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a business performs two different kinds of work under one contract and invoices a customer in another city. The bookkeeper saves the scope, location, billing detail and certificate support, then asks the preparer whether separate TPT classifications or local treatment apply. No tax rate or classification result is assumed.

At year end, assemble reconciliations, activity schedules, asset records, payroll annual totals, returns and unresolved notices. Contractors, retailers and specialized services may require different treatment. Paper Trail can organize and reconcile the evidence; a qualified tax professional or attorney must resolve uncertain tax and employment positions before filing.

sections.heading: DFA Registration And Local Tax Records
paragraphs: Arkansas DFA's sales/use section issues tax permits and administers state sales/use together with city and county local option taxes and other specified programs. Keep each account, business location, legal name, ownership change and assigned filing schedule in one register. A change of activity can require more review than simply editing a website description.

Retain the permit and agency acknowledgments, not just a login. ATAP provides an access point for tax accounts, but it does not decide the treatment of every sale. Give the qualified preparer product descriptions, delivery destinations and employee locations for nexus and account review.

sections.heading: Sales, Exemptions And Vendor Purchases
paragraphs: Preserve gross sales, refunds, tax charged, location evidence and exemption support in a transaction file. Sales tax, use tax and local reporting should remain distinguishable even if a software export combines them. Use the current rules for the actual goods or services rather than assuming all business transactions qualify as resale.

For accounts payable, save invoices showing what was purchased, where used and any tax charged. DFA's FAQ identifies specific local tax issues on qualifying business purchases. Such relief is not an automatic deduction from every supplier invoice; preserve evidence and obtain preparer approval before claiming a credit or refund. Separate equipment, inventory and operating supplies.

sections.heading: Withholding Records And Unemployment
paragraphs: DFA's withholding instructions specify records including wage payment dates, employee certificates, deposits and annual reconciliation confirmations, with at least six years of state withholding records. Keep these materials with the reporting period and distinguish withholding from company wage expense. A payroll bank withdrawal alone does not prove a return was filed.

The workforce agency separately provides unemployment employer accounts and Tax 21. Covered employers pay unemployment tax on payroll quarterly. Keep rate notices, wage detail, reports, amendments and payment confirmations independently of the DFA account. Resolve worker status and multistate work with a payroll specialist rather than making an assumption from an invoice label.

sections.heading: Income Evidence And Monthly Statements
paragraphs: These are general accounting recommendations. Match customer receipts to invoices, separate owner funding and borrowing from sales, reconcile cards/banks and review outstanding supplier balances. Record credits against the correct original transaction so income and expenses are not understated by unexplained net entries.

Build liability schedules for state/local sales and use tax, employee withholding and employer payroll charges that apply. Each should explain beginning balance, additions, payments and ending balance. Show cash commitments for taxes and unpaid bills alongside customer aging so a profitable month is not mistaken for spendable cash.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Illustration: A Mixed Purchase Invoice
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a company buys merchandise for resale and a fixture for its store on the same supplier invoice. The bookkeeper retains item descriptions, resale documentation, delivery location and amounts assigned to each purpose. The preparer reviews tax treatment by item instead of marking the whole bill exempt.

If a local tax credit or refund may apply, preserve the source invoice, payment and written analysis with the claim. Do not reduce current tax payable based on an owner's recollection of an earlier purchase. The illustration supplies no rate, eligibility conclusion or credit amount.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And Elective Entity Tax
paragraphs: Arkansas provides corporation income tax filing through ATAP and a separate elective entity tax for eligible partnerships, S corporations and LLCs. DFA states that this election is not available to sole proprietors, trusts, C corporations or LLCs taxed as C corporations. Preserve the federal classification and election documents. Payroll withholding and owner related tax payments must remain distinguishable even when both pass through ATAP.

The accounting file should retain income and deductions, asset schedules, Arkansas and other state activity, owner allocations and the federal return. Use a separate monthly schedule for corporate or elected entity estimates and credits and retain the preparer calculation supporting any provision. At year end hand over election evidence, payments by tax year, ownership changes, distributions and tax adjustment workpapers. Keep payments on behalf of owners traceable to each owner rather than burying them in wages or general taxes.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Arkansas rule 11 CAR 1-205 requires quarterly contribution and wage reporting for employers within its scope, including employers electing reimbursement instead of regular contributions. The rule directs electronic reporting through the Workforce Services portal. Keep the reporting account type, quarterly employee wage file and contribution or reimbursement evidence. Reconcile the liability against accepted reports and actual payments rather than only the payroll provider withdrawal. Preserve corrections by their original reporting period and include the quarterly reconciliation in the annual payroll package.

sections.heading: Year End Preparation, Retention And Industry Scope
paragraphs: Give the CPA or enrolled agent reconciled balances, sales/use filings, payroll annual totals, asset acquisitions/disposals, open customer and supplier items and unresolved notices. Preserve entity changes and prior tax adjustments for state income or other entity filing review. Filing duties depend on the legal entity and activity, not just the trade name.

Apply the verified six year withholding period only to its stated scope. Establish separate documented periods for sales/use, unemployment, assets and federal records; this resource does not invent those periods. Extend preservation for audits or disputes. Retail, rental, tourism and specialized sales may require different review under DFA programs. Bookkeeping support is not tax filing or legal advice.

sections.heading: State Collected And Self Collected Jurisdictions
paragraphs: Colorado DOR administers state sales tax and many local taxes, but some home rule cities administer their own. DOR's state sales publication does not automatically describe those cities' rules. Keep addresses, delivery evidence, business locations and a jurisdiction register for the person preparing returns.

Use current local contacts and DOR resources to confirm accounts and assigned filing periods. A single portal or software rate table is not proof that every local obligation has been reviewed. Preserve any local registration and correspondence separately from the state account so a change in address does not erase earlier reporting history.

sections.heading: Sales, Certificates And Use Tax Purchases
paragraphs: Retain gross sales, taxable and exempt detail, customer refunds, delivery destination and certificates. DOR describes taxability of goods, specified services and some mixed transactions; bundled work needs factual review. Preserve invoice components rather than assigning an exemption because the seller calls itself a service business.

For payables, identify equipment and supplies used by the business with no tax charged. Keep invoices, use locations and the reason for any claimed exemption. SUTS has distinct handling and limitations for state collected consumer use tax, according to its FAQ. Do not assume filing sales through SUTS automatically settles every purchase use tax responsibility.

sections.heading: Payroll And Separate Program Evidence
paragraphs: Colorado DOR provides withholding registration, payment, annual reconciliation and wage statement resources. Keep employee forms, work locations, payroll registers, deposit confirmations and filed annual totals. Reconcile state withholding separately from employer expense and from unemployment.

FAMLI is another program, with employer wage reporting and premiums subject to applicable coverage rules. Save the approval documentation for any private plan and confirm who submits required summaries. A payroll provider's combined debit should be supported by program level reports. Ask a specialist to determine coverage, worker classification and any local payroll obligations.

sections.heading: Retention And Software Changes
paragraphs: For state and state administered sales tax, DOR specifies at least three years of necessary books and records, including resale purchase invoices and sufficient exemption evidence. That minimum does not establish retention for self collected cities, employment records, federal taxes, property basis or open disputes.

Maintain an agency specific schedule and obtain professional confirmation before deleting records. Test exports from sales and payroll systems before switching providers. Keep transaction identifiers and code explanations so an earlier exempt amount can be connected to the original invoice without reconstructing it from a summary spreadsheet.

sections.heading: Monthly Reporting And A Delivery Example
paragraphs: General monthly practice is to reconcile banks and cards, review supplier/customer aging and explain financing and owner transactions. Maintain tax liabilities by reporting authority, with cash payments applied to the correct period. An unexplained difference between the sales system and revenue should remain on a review list.

Hypothetical example: a seller delivers orders into two Colorado cities, one self collected. The bookkeeper preserves each destination, invoice, refund and exemption document, then the preparer checks the appropriate authority and rule. The example does not assume equal local treatment or a universal rate. Processor settlement fees remain separate from gross sales.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And SALT Parity Records
paragraphs: Colorado corporate income tax and the SALT Parity election require their own accounting support. Revenue describes the election as an annual choice for partnerships and S corporations to pay Colorado income tax at the entity level. It is binding for the elected period, with specified owner exceptions. Preserve the signed decision, entity classification and owner details instead of assuming every partnership has made the election.

Maintain state income adjustments, Colorado source income and resident versus nonresident owner allocations for the preparer. When estimates apply, track entity payments and credits separately from personal owner estimates, sales tax and payroll. At the monthly close, reconcile payments to the correct tax year and keep the provision tied to the latest approved computation. Include the election, owner schedules, state adjustments and prior credits in the annual handoff so the entity payment and owner reporting agree.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Colorado requires liable employers to provide quarterly wage detail and monthly employment data, with unemployment premiums handled through MyUI Employer+. Preserve the wage file, monthly counts, premium calculation and amendments as a distinct payroll workpaper. Reconcile the employer premium accrued in the ledger to accepted reports, posted payments and the assigned notice. Include those reports and the ending payable in the annual handoff, with any quarter corrected after the books closed. Keep unemployment controls separate from FAMLI contributions and state withholding.

sections.heading: Year End And Professional Review
paragraphs: At year end, organize state and local filings, FAMLI and unemployment reports, wage statements, asset support, account reconciliations and unresolved notices. Record locations added or closed during the year. Give entity/election and ownership documentation to the tax professional for income tax review.

Retailers, mobile vendors, mixed service sellers and contractors can have different sourcing and licensing facts. This resource does not resolve nexus or any particular city's law. Paper Trail's bookkeeping support can preserve evidence and make reports understandable; a qualified preparer, payroll expert or attorney must decide uncertain tax and employment positions.

sections.heading: DRS Accounts And Business Registration
paragraphs: Connecticut DRS uses myconneCT for registering and managing tax accounts. Keep the legal entity, registration number, locations, activities and authorized contacts in an accessible register. Selling taxable goods or services can require a sales/use permit; a temporary event does not automatically remove that requirement.

Add withholding as a separate tax account when applicable. DRS's new employer information also identifies separate Department of Labor unemployment registration. A business can use the same payroll provider without those registrations becoming interchangeable. Confirm the entity's income or other business tax filings with its tax professional.

sections.heading: Sales And Business Use Purchases
paragraphs: Preserve itemized sales, tax charged, taxable versus exempt detail and delivery evidence. Connecticut taxes specified services as well as many goods, including certain digital products. Keep exemption and resale documents linked to the customer and transaction rather than applying an unsupported exemption to the entire customer account.

Review supplier invoices for purchases used by the business without tax charged. Retain the item description, use location, date and payment for business use tax evaluation. A resale purchase later consumed by the business needs review; a certificate does not make every acquisition permanently exempt. Payable credits should retain a connection to the original invoice.

sections.heading: Withholding, Unemployment And Paid Leave
paragraphs: Maintain withholding certificates, wage registers, filings and payment confirmations, and reconcile DRS withholding separately from Department of Labor unemployment. Actual work/residence circumstances can affect payroll treatment, so preserve them for the specialist. Do not infer correct reporting from the employee's net paycheck.

CT Paid Leave is separately administered. Its employer resource describes covered employer registration, employee deductions and quarterly remittance, even where a provider assists. Keep the account registration, deduction detail, submitted data and contributions distinct from income tax withholding. Eligibility, exemptions and private plans need a specialist's review; this resource supplies no contribution rate.

sections.heading: Retention By Document Type
paragraphs: DRS's information return instructions require Connecticut information return records for at least four years after the due date. Its Getting Started in Business publication describes six years for seller transaction and resale records. Because an older companion presentation gives a different minimum/recommendation distinction, confirm the current governing rule with DRS before adopting a destruction schedule.

Do not treat a four year information return rule as permission to delete all payroll, leave, asset or sales records. Preserve open audit/dispute evidence longer, and retain source files in a format that can be read after a software change. A dated retention policy should identify each agency and document category.

sections.heading: Monthly Statements And An Event Example
paragraphs: The monthly accounting routine is general practice: reconcile cash/cards, match receipts to invoices, review unpaid bills and separate borrowing or owner funding from revenue. Roll tax and payroll liabilities forward by program. Show actual remittances and timing differences instead of zeroing an account to make the statement appear complete.

Hypothetical example: a Connecticut business sells products at a weekend event and also invoices for a separately described service. The bookkeeper retains the permit information, sales detail, location, refunds and service contract. The preparer evaluates the taxability of each activity; no rate or blanket service exemption is assumed. Net card deposits are reconciled to gross activity and fees.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Corporation Business Tax And Optional Entity Tax
paragraphs: Connecticut corporation business tax and optional entity tax have separate filing frameworks. DRS explains that qualifying partnerships and S corporations with Connecticut business or source income may elect the PE Tax annually; it is optional rather than an automatic charge on every LLC. Preserve the election, federal classification, member information and the composite return records used with that election.

Keep Connecticut income allocation and state adjustments with the federal business return, and retain member residence and ownership changes. Reconcile any corporation business or elected PE estimates, return payments and credits in distinct monthly schedules. At year end give the preparer the election, prior payments, ownership allocations, assets and federal adjustment evidence. A corporation in a related group may need combined reporting analysis; the bookkeeper should preserve ownership and intercompany records without deciding the group conclusion.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Connecticut Labor identifies employers liable for unemployment coverage and directs quarterly tax and wage reports and contributions through ReEmployCT. Maintain its Employer Account Number separately from DRS and Paid Leave registrations. Match employee quarterly wage detail to payroll, then reconcile employer contribution accruals to the report, posted payments and account credits. Retain benefit charge correspondence for review because it can affect future experience rates. The annual package should contain four quarterly files, corrections and the closing unemployment payable, separate from Paid Leave deductions.

sections.heading: Year End And Scope Of Advice
paragraphs: Prepare the annual package with reconciliations, receivables/payables, business use purchase reviews, payroll and Paid Leave totals, asset transactions and filed confirmations. DRS provides annual withholding reconciliation and wage statement requirements; compare provider annual totals with the periodic records before submission.

Contractors, retailers, digital sellers and professional firms can need different reviews. This resource does not decide nexus, worker classification, entity elections or private plan eligibility. A qualified tax or payroll professional should resolve those issues. Paper Trail's role is accurate bookkeeping and support for the decision, not a legal conclusion or promise of compliance.

sections.heading: Gross Receipts And Delivery Evidence
paragraphs: Delaware does not impose the usual retail sales tax. Its gross receipts tax instead falls on the seller and depends on business activity. Revenue explains that ordinary costs such as merchandise, labor and interest do not reduce the gross receipts tax base. Preserve gross receipts before supplier bills or processing costs are deducted, and distinguish activity categories for the preparer.

Revenue distinguishes goods shipped directly to customers outside Delaware from retail goods picked up within Delaware. Keep the customer invoice and shipping evidence together. Certain wholesale pickups have a separate Form 373 exemption process; do not apply that treatment to every customer who says the goods will leave the state. These distinctions make delivery documentation part of the accounting file.

sections.heading: Employer Accounts And Paid Leave
paragraphs: Withholding belongs to the Division of Revenue, while unemployment reporting is a Department of Labor responsibility. Maintain employee withholding certificates, payroll registers, agency confirmations and rate correspondence by program. The Revenue employer publication requires pertinent withholding records for at least three years from filing the annual reconciliation. Its older form and filing references require comparison with current instructions.

Delaware Paid Leave became fully effective in 2026. Participating employers report hours and wages quarterly through LaborFirst, including applicable private plan employers. Keep coverage decisions, employee hours, payroll deductions, employer contributions and confirmations separately from unemployment. Do not infer an exemption merely because the business has a private policy or uses a payroll provider.

sections.heading: Purchases, Payables And Operating Results
paragraphs: As general bookkeeping practice, pair every supplier bill with approval, receiving evidence and payment. Distinguish stock acquired for customers from equipment used by the business. Retain freight bills and credit memos so inventory cost and outstanding payables can be explained. A supplier charge should remain visible even when a processor or platform deducts it from a customer payout.

Classify customer receipts, borrowing and owner funding by their underlying documents. Review deposits and refunds against open invoices rather than treating every bank credit as sales. Track operating expenses for profitability and the income tax handoff even when those expenses do not reduce gross receipts tax. Preserve contracts for deposits and advance payments so the accounting basis can be applied consistently.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Monthly Reports And Reconciliations
paragraphs: A useful monthly close reconciles banks, cards and merchant clearing accounts, then reviews receivables, unpaid supplier bills and inventory adjustments. Produce a profit and loss statement and balance sheet on the agreed accounting basis. Add a cash forecast when major stock orders or payroll payments are approaching; accounting profit does not establish available cash.

Maintain a separate movement schedule for gross receipts tax, withholding, unemployment and Paid Leave where applicable. Show the opening amount, current activity, payments and closing amount. Compare submitted reports with the ledger and identify payments still clearing. Investigate a provider debit that covers several programs before assigning the whole amount to payroll expense.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Year End And Record Preservation
paragraphs: For the tax preparer, assemble annual receipts by activity, shipping support, payroll totals, agency payment histories, asset purchases and disposals, inventory counts, financing agreements and owner transactions. Explain why gross receipts filings differ from financial statement revenue when timing or classification differs. Keep a list of unresolved adjustments and prior filing changes.

The verified three year period concerns Delaware withholding records and starts with the annual reconciliation filing. This research did not establish one destruction date for gross receipts, corporate, unemployment and Paid Leave files. Use a document specific policy, preserve unresolved assessments and consult the preparer before deleting source records. Maintain accessible exports when changing software.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And Owner Tax Records
paragraphs: Delaware Revenue requires nonexempt corporations doing business in Delaware to file corporate income returns, while recognizing different treatment for S corporation income. S corporations with Delaware source income have an information return and payments on behalf of nonresident shareholders to consider. Preserve classification elections, actual operating locations and ownership details; Delaware incorporation alone does not settle the income tax answer.

For monthly bookkeeping, separate gross receipts tax from corporate income estimates and payments made for owners. Retain receipt sourcing, state adjustments, prior credits and the preparer calculation supporting an accrual. At year end provide the federal business return, Delaware activity, owner residence and distribution records, estimates and filed acknowledgments. Corporate franchise or entity registration charges need their own records and review; the absence of ordinary sales tax does not remove those separate obligations.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Delaware Labor requires quarterly reports distinguishing total gross wages and taxable wages for unemployment. Its FAQ has inconsistent wage base figures, so use the current year assigned notice and instructions rather than copying those figures. Reconcile employer contributions to the quarterly wage file, posted agency payment and ledger payable. Keep benefit charge notices and wage corrections with the affected quarter. Annual payroll support should include those reconciliations in addition to the separate Paid Leave hours and wage files.

sections.heading: A Wilmington Order Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Wilmington retailer sells one order collected at its shop and another shipped by the retailer to a Maryland customer. The bookkeeper stores the pickup receipt for the first order and carrier proof for the second, while recording both sales before card fees. The preparer evaluates gross receipts reporting from those different delivery facts. Purchasing the merchandise remains an operating cost, rather than an automatic gross receipts deduction.

sections.heading: Sales Tax And Purchase Review
paragraphs: Georgia requires a dealer to retain sales and purchase records, accounting books and invoices needed to determine sales and use tax for no less than three years. Registered filers must submit a return even when there were no sales or no tax due. Preserve the activity behind a zero return so an inactive month can be distinguished from a missed filing.

Build the sales detail from customer invoices or register exports rather than the bank deposit. Retain tax collected, returns, delivery information and documents supporting resale or other exempt treatment. The department provides ST-3 return instructions with local reporting detail. Keep transactions assigned to their actual jurisdictions and let the preparer resolve questionable sourcing or taxable services.

sections.heading: Withholding And Unemployment Documentation
paragraphs: Revenue identifies Form G-4 for employee withholding and G-1003 for income statement reporting. Keep certificates, pay dates, wage totals and withheld amounts linked to the employer account. Retain filing acknowledgments and compare payroll service reports with amounts actually paid to Revenue. Nonresident owner withholding is a separate issue from employee payroll.

The Department of Labor handles unemployment wage and tax reporting through its employer services. Keep the Labor account number, assigned notices, employee wage detail, quarterly reports and payment receipts together. Reconcile the unemployment balance independently of Revenue withholding, even when one payroll service withdraws cash for both. Worker classification and wages spanning several states need professional review.

sections.heading: Vendor Bills And Income Evidence
paragraphs: General bookkeeping practice calls for an approved bill, evidence of receipt and payment for each supplier purchase. Capture the place the item was delivered and whether tax was charged. Flag equipment, subscriptions and supplies with uncertain tax treatment for review rather than assuming every expense from a distant vendor is exempt. Preserve vendor credits against the original purchase.

Maintain separate accounts for merchandise cost, services purchased, equipment and owner spending. For income, connect invoices, customer deposits, refunds and processor deductions to the contract or sale. If financing arrives in the operating account, attach the loan agreement and record principal separately from revenue. These distinctions improve both financial reports and the preparer handoff.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Monthly Financial Review
paragraphs: Reconcile banks, cards and payment processors each month, including fees, chargebacks and settlements received after the sale. Review unpaid invoices and supplier balances for errors and duplicate payments. Produce the profit and loss statement, balance sheet and a list of upcoming cash commitments. These are recommended accounting routines, rather than a Georgia filing rule.

Prepare a sales tax reconciliation from gross sales through supported exclusions to reported taxable activity and tax. Keep withholding and unemployment movement schedules beside it. Each should show accrued amounts, agency payments, credits and unresolved differences. An automatic payment does not prove that the return was accepted or that it used the correct period.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention
paragraphs: Give the tax preparer the annual trial balance, reconciliations, sales tax summaries, payroll and G-1003 support, unemployment reports, inventory counts and asset schedules. Include vendor payment detail, financing statements and owner transactions. Explain unusual refunds or changes in sales channels so the preparer can assess information reporting and income tax treatment.

The verified Georgia minimum of three years applies to sales and use tax books and records. It is not a universal period for employment documents, property basis or every federal return. Preserve records involved in an audit or disputed treatment and retain usable exports after replacing a point of sale or accounting system. Confirm other retention categories before destruction.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And Net Worth Evidence
paragraphs: Georgia distinguishes corporate income tax from corporate net worth tax. Income tax uses federal taxable income with Georgia adjustments, while net worth reporting needs balance sheet and entity information. Revenue states an LLC is subject to net worth tax only when treated as a corporation for income tax purposes. Retain the federal election and state classification rather than assessing this tax merely because the name ends in LLC.

Keep Georgia and total receipts, asset locations, capital contributions and retained earnings support for the preparer. The corporate net worth period can differ from the income tax period, so label estimates, final payments and credits by both tax type and year in monthly reconciliations. The annual package should include the opening and closing balance sheets, initial or final entity changes, federal return, apportionment data and prior net worth filings. A loss in operations does not establish that every corporate reporting duty has ended.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Georgia Labor uses quarterly tax and employee wage reporting for unemployment, with the employer account and assigned rate separate from Revenue withholding. Preserve the taxable wage calculation and notices that explain the contribution amount rather than reconciling only gross payroll. Each month roll employer unemployment expense and unpaid contributions forward and match payments to accepted reports. Include corrections and benefit charge correspondence in the annual file so the preparer can trace changes affecting the employer account.

A new display cabinet invoice with unclear tax is placed in the purchase review file for the preparer.

sections.heading: General Excise And Use Tax Records
paragraphs: Hawaii general excise tax is a business activity tax rather than a conventional retail sales tax. The current state brochure describes periodic G-45 returns and an annual G-49 reconciliation. Organize gross income by business activity, preserve claimed exemption evidence and keep location detail needed for county allocation. A single total of bank deposits cannot establish those categories.

The same brochure addresses use tax on imports. Retain supplier invoices, freight documents, what was imported and how the business used it. Classify stock for resale separately from equipment and supplies for internal use, then give uncertain treatment to the preparer. A charge described as tax on a supplier bill needs identification before being treated as satisfaction of Hawaii obligations.

sections.heading: Payroll And Employer Insurance
paragraphs: Keep the Hawaii withholding account, employee certificates, registers and payment confirmations distinct from the unemployment account. DOTAX lists HW-14 periodic withholding returns and wage statements. Its current forms list marks HW-3 obsolete for years beginning in 2020, although some explanatory pages still refer to it. Use the current year instructions when preparing annual submissions.

Hawaii Labor administers unemployment separately from Temporary Disability Insurance and Prepaid Health Care. Maintain hours, wages, coverage records, insurer bills and authorized deductions so a specialist can evaluate employee eligibility and the employer share. Reconcile insurance payables to insurer statements rather than including every benefit withdrawal in one tax account. The programs have different purposes and coverage conditions.

sections.heading: Purchases And Operating Expenses
paragraphs: As a practical accounting routine, match the purchase order or approval, invoice, shipping bill and payment. Island freight can make the amount paid differ from the supplier product price. Preserve the components so inventory and equipment cost can be evaluated. Keep damaged shipment credits attached to the original transaction instead of deleting the original invoice.

Track customer deposits, completed work, refunds, loans and owner contributions separately. Record processor fees using settlement detail while retaining gross customer activity. Classify rent, insurance and service costs with business purpose evidence, and hold personal transactions in an owner account for review. Profitability reporting and general excise reporting can require different presentations of the same activity.

sections.heading: Monthly Close And Cash Planning
paragraphs: Recommended monthly reports include a reconciled balance sheet, profit and loss statement, receivable and payable aging, and a cash forecast for freight, payroll and upcoming tax payments. Reconcile bank, card and processor accounts before interpreting operating margins. Investigate deposits that cover several customer orders or several business activities.

Use distinct liability schedules for general excise/use tax, withholding, unemployment and applicable insurance deductions. Compare payroll and hours with submitted reports, then compare agency and insurer payments with the ledger. Explain differences between periodic general excise returns and the annual workpaper as they arise rather than reconstructing an entire year later.

sections.heading: Annual Handoff And Record Retention
paragraphs: Prepare G-49 support from the periodic returns, gross receipts detail and exemption schedules. Give the tax preparer the annual trial balance, bank reconciliations, asset and import records, inventory counts, payroll statements, insurance reconciliations and financing agreements. Highlight corrections and unresolved island or activity allocations.

The state general excise brochure requires relevant records in English within Hawaii for at least three years, including gross income and exemption support. That requirement does not settle every payroll, insurance or property retention period. Preserve open disputes and records with continuing basis relevance, and confirm storage arrangements before relying solely on a cloud account.

sections.heading: Income Tax Beside General Excise Tax
paragraphs: Hawaii corporate income reporting is separate from general excise tax. Current N-30 instructions identify corporate filing for Hawaii source gross income, subject to exemptions, and direct corporations with a valid federal S election to N-35. DOTAX also provides an elective entity tax for qualifying partnerships and S corporations. Preserve the classification and any approved election rather than treating GET registration as the income tax determination.

Keep income and deduction detail, asset basis, Hawaii adjustments and allocation workpapers, with owner records where income passes to owners. Reconcile corporate or elected entity estimates separately from G-45 remittances during the monthly close. The annual handoff should include federal return support, state asset differences, payments by year, N-20 or N-35 evidence where relevant and the election forms. A business with little profit can still have substantial gross activity for GET, so the two calculations should remain independently traceable.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Hawaii Labor says liable employers must submit an unemployment report every quarter even when no workers were paid or the tax cannot be paid. Keep the liability determination, wages by employee, contribution calculation and accepted report. Reconcile the employer contribution payable independently from withheld income tax, TDI and health plan deductions, and retain evidence for a zero wage quarter. Include quarterly filings, corrections and unresolved notices in the annual payroll package so an unpaid balance is visible rather than concealed by the absence of a bank payment.

sections.heading: A Maui Business Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Maui business sells locally made products and imports display equipment from the mainland. The bookkeeper separates gross product receipts from processor fees, retains shipment and equipment invoices, and lists the import for use tax review. Employee hours and benefit deductions are reconciled independently of general excise filings. The preparer determines the applicable activities and tax treatment.

sections.heading: Sales, Exemptions And Purchases
paragraphs: The Tax Commission specifies gross receipts, untaxed sales, customer exemption identities, purchase prices and tax collected or paid among records to preserve. Delivery proof matters when goods go somewhere other than the seller location. Keep invoice detail and credit memos linked to the sale so reported revenue and tax can be reconstructed without relying on a net bank payout.

For supplier purchases, capture the product, delivery location, business purpose and tax line. Separate goods bought for resale, items rented to customers and equipment consumed by the business. Put purchases without clear tax treatment on a review schedule. Exemption certificates need a connection to actual customers and transactions rather than a folder of unrelated documents.

sections.heading: Payroll Reconciliation And Labor Records
paragraphs: Idaho Form 967 reconciles income tax withheld, payments forwarded to the Tax Commission and withholding shown on wage or information statements. The agency says the 2025 Form 967 onward is filed online through TAP. Keep employee registers and payment detail that allow those three totals to be compared; investigate corrections and missing payments rather than entering a balancing adjustment.

The Department of Labor provides a separate unemployment wage reporting and tax payment system. Preserve account correspondence, employee wage detail, filed reports and payment confirmations by quarter. Retain worker agreements and work locations for classification or multistate review. A contractor invoice or information return alone does not settle whether the worker belongs on payroll.

sections.heading: Vendor Balances And Operating Income
paragraphs: General bookkeeping practice starts each payable with a vendor invoice and evidence that goods or services were received. Match discounts and credits before payment, and reconcile recurring supplier statements to the ledger. For equipment financed by a dealer, retain both the asset invoice and financing agreement so the purchase is not reduced to a monthly expense.

Distinguish customer revenue from loan proceeds and owner funding. Match customer advances to contracts and track refunds against the original sale. A business selling products and performing work should retain descriptions of each activity for tax review and management reporting. Preserve inventory counts, writeoffs and goods removed for business or personal use.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Monthly Reports And Annual Preparation
paragraphs: Recommended monthly reports include the profit and loss statement, balance sheet, receivable and payable aging, and reconciled inventory where relevant. Reconcile banks, cards and processor clearing accounts first. Roll sales/use tax, withholding and unemployment balances forward separately with the opening amount, accruals, payments and ending balance.

Give the preparer annual reconciliations, sales and exemption detail, purchase tax questions, payroll and Form 967 support, unemployment reports, asset additions and disposals, financing balances and owner transactions. Include a separate list of corrections and uncertain classifications. Periodic reports should explain timing differences rather than hiding them in miscellaneous expense.

sections.heading: Retention And Usable Exports
paragraphs: The verified Tax Commission recordkeeping page states at least four years for sales and use records and seven years when there is no Idaho seller permit number. It also says resale or exemption certificates should be kept while the buyer remains a customer plus four years. Apply those categories individually rather than deleting all evidence after a customer leaves.

The cited page addresses wholesalers and related sales/use evidence; confirm the exact rule for the business and other tax programs before destroying records. Keep open assessment evidence and continuing property basis documents longer where needed. Export invoices, certificates, registers and return workpapers in a readable format before closing a software account.

sections.heading: Partnership Income And Owner Payment Choices
paragraphs: Idaho requires Form 65 for partnerships doing business in Idaho, including LLCs treated as partnerships. The Tax Commission describes nonresident individual owner withholding, composite reporting and signed owner agreements as different paths. Preserve owner residence, ownership percentages and the actual agreement or reporting decision; none of those payments belongs in employee payroll merely because it is called withholding.

Idaho also offers the affected business entity election, and a July 2026 agency announcement describes changed election timing. Keep current year election evidence with the preparer approval. Reconcile owner withholding, composite or elected entity tax payments by program and tax year at month end. At year end provide federal return support, Idaho source income, capital changes, owner agreements and payment histories so the preparer can produce the owner schedules and assess the current election rules.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Idaho Labor requires quarterly unemployment reports even when no wages were paid and directs employers to online reporting unless paper permission is granted. Errors must be corrected in the quarter where they occurred. Use wage records and the current rate notice to support employer contribution calculations, independently of TAP income tax. During monthly reconciliation distinguish gross payroll from wages used for contributions, and match accepted filings with posted payments. The annual handoff should retain quarterly reports, amendments and benefit correspondence rather than substituting income tax withholding records for unemployment evidence.

sections.heading: A Boise Wholesale Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Boise wholesaler sells to a reseller and also withdraws stock to furnish its own office. The bookkeeper stores the reseller certificate and delivery record with customer sales, while documenting the stock withdrawal and original cost separately. The preparer reviews the internal use transaction. The same month payroll withholding is compared with payments and statement totals for Form 967 support.

sections.heading: Retail Records And Transaction Locations
paragraphs: Illinois Publication 113 requires retailers to preserve sales, purchases, inventory changes, receivables, payables and return workpapers. It also emphasizes location support for destination transactions. Retain customer delivery addresses and shipment origins where applicable, with gross sales detail and tax. An order assigned only to a postal code can leave the actual destination unresolved.

Link exemption support to individual sales, leases or rentals, including the purchaser, transaction character, date and receipts. For supplier bills, record whether purchases are stock, equipment or supplies and preserve the tax charged. Separate questionable untaxed purchases for use tax review. Inventory records should explain transfers, shrinkage and goods removed from stock.

sections.heading: Withholding Dates And Unemployment
paragraphs: Form IL-941 instructions require Illinois withholding to be reported on the date payroll or compensation was paid, rather than the later tax deposit date. Preserve pay dates and tax by payroll run. Schedule P and any applicable credit schedule are part of the return support. Reconcile withheld amounts independently from gross wages and employer payroll costs.

IDES administers unemployment reports separately from Revenue withholding. Its resources cover quarterly contributions and additional monthly wage reporting for qualifying employers. Maintain the IDES account, rate notices, wage files and acknowledgments. MyTax Illinois access can cover both programs, but a contribution payment and a monthly wage report serve different purposes.

sections.heading: Accounts Payable And Income Evidence
paragraphs: For management accounting, reconcile vendor statements to open bills before payment. Attach purchase approvals, delivery receipts, credit memos and settlement evidence. Equipment leases and installment contracts should retain their original agreements; a bank debit alone may combine principal, interest, insurance and fees.

Separate customer receipts, advance payments, borrowing and owner contributions. Preserve sales channel reports before processing fees, and connect refunds to the original transactions. For businesses that both sell goods and provide services, descriptions of what was transferred and where it was delivered give the preparer better evidence than one undifferentiated revenue account.

sections.heading: Monthly Statements And Closing Controls
paragraphs: Recommended monthly controls include bank and card reconciliations, processor settlement checks, receivable and payable aging, and review of inventory and asset activity. Present a profit and loss statement and balance sheet with unresolved items identified. Large receivables or seasonal stock purchases may also justify a short cash forecast.

Maintain separate schedules for sales/use tax, income tax withholding and unemployment contributions. Match the return periods, payment dates and agency credits to the ledger. Retain filed returns and supporting exports so an amended filing can be traced to the original calculation. Do not clear an agency balance merely because a payroll service has withdrawn cash.

sections.heading: Annual Handoff And Retention
paragraphs: Prepare the tax handoff with the annual trial balance, reconciliations, location based sales summaries, exemption evidence, purchase tax review, payroll returns, wage statements and IDES reports. Add physical inventory, asset changes, loan balances and owner transactions. Compare annual statement totals with the periodic withholding records and explain every correction.

Publication 113 generally requires receipts documentation for three and one half years after the original or amended return is filed. Records related to an issued tax liability or final notice must remain until the liability is finalized or discharged. The publication also sets access, readability, English language and Illinois storage requirements unless written permission allows another location. Confirm how those conditions apply to electronic storage.

sections.heading: Income, Replacement And Elected Entity Taxes
paragraphs: Illinois business taxation includes replacement tax as well as corporate income tax. Publication 129 explains that partnerships and S corporations can have replacement tax on Illinois income even when ordinary income passes to their owners. It also distinguishes an optional PTE tax election from withholding for nonresident members. Retain the entity classification, election and member exemption documents rather than treating all state income payments as one owner distribution.

Maintain state adjustments, receipts sourcing, member allocations and federal return support. Reconcile replacement tax, applicable corporate income tax and elected entity or owner withholding payments separately during the monthly close. At year end give the preparer the payment history, credit carryforwards, ownership changes and Illinois member schedules. Compare credits reported to owners with the entity workpapers; a state payment can support an owner credit without representing employee withholding or satisfying replacement tax.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: IDES distinguishes quarterly contribution reports, which calculate unemployment contributions, from additional monthly wage reports that do not calculate or remit contributions. Preserve the employer reporting determination and the applicable wage files so a monthly upload is not mistaken for the quarterly tax return. Reconcile employer contribution expense, agency credits and payments to the quarterly liability. At year end provide all required reports and amendments with annual payroll totals, while keeping the monthly information submissions separately identifiable.

sections.heading: A Rockford Delivery Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Rockford retailer delivers one order to a customer facility and allows another customer to collect an order. The bookkeeper retains exact delivery evidence for the first and pickup evidence for the second, with the order and gross payment detail. The preparer determines sourcing. Payroll issued at month end is recorded by pay date even if the tax deposit settles the following month.

sections.heading: Sales, Purchases And Tax Accounts
paragraphs: Indiana DOR describes sales and withholding filing through electronic services and issues a Registered Retail Merchant Certificate after the business tax registration process. Preserve the registration and actual account details rather than using entity formation documents as evidence that tax accounts are open.

The DOR audit manual identifies sales invoices, point of sale records, return calculations and exemption support as sales tax evidence. Its use tax discussion emphasizes retaining the purchases on which tax was reported. Keep vendor invoices, delivery locations, items purchased and tax treatment with the workpaper. A total use tax payment cannot explain which purchases it covers.

sections.heading: State And County Payroll Evidence
paragraphs: Indiana WH-3 reconciles state and county income taxes withheld during the year. Retain employee WH-4 certificates, payroll registers, tax detail and remittance confirmations so county amounts can be compared with the provider records. Review certificate changes and uncertain residency facts with the payroll professional rather than assuming a mailing address resolves county withholding.

DWD unemployment wage reports use a separate employer account and reporting process. Its current employer page announces enhanced wage fields beginning with fourth quarter 2026 reports, including job titles, hours paid and reporting unit information. Review provider readiness before that report. Preserve the wage files, filed acknowledgments and employer contribution notices independently of DOR withholding.

sections.heading: Vendor Documents And Income Classification
paragraphs: As a general accounting routine, match vendor bills with approval, delivery and payment, and use supplier statements to catch missing credits or duplicate bills. Distinguish inventory from equipment, and retain financing agreements for installment purchases. Document stock withdrawn for the business or owner instead of treating it as an unexplained inventory difference.

Match customer invoices, deposits, refunds and merchant settlements to their source transactions. Separate loans and owner funds from revenue and separate principal repayment from interest. Keep the contract for customer advances so the agreed accounting basis can be applied. If projects span months, preserve job costs and amounts billed to explain margin movements.

sections.heading: Monthly Close And Financial Reports
paragraphs: Recommended monthly reports include a reconciled profit and loss statement, balance sheet, receivable and payable aging, and project or inventory detail where useful. Reconcile cash, cards and processor balances, review stale clearing entries and investigate negative customer or vendor balances. A transfer between business accounts should not inflate sales or expenses.

Prepare separate schedules for sales/use tax, state withholding, county withholding and unemployment. Compare report totals with ledger accruals and payments, and document timing differences at month end. Retain agency credits and amendments in the same period file so the next close starts from a supported opening balance.

sections.heading: Annual Preparation And Retention
paragraphs: Deliver the annual trial balance, reconciliations, sales and use tax calculations, exemption files, WH-3 support, payroll statements and unemployment reports to the preparer. Add inventory counts, asset transactions, financing balances and owner activity. Flag missing certificates and any enhanced wage data that the provider cannot yet produce.

The current DOR business handbook says to keep use tax transaction documents, accrual records, returns and asset support for at least three years in addition to the current year, and longer for pending proceedings or appeals. This verified category is not permission to discard every payroll or property document at that point. Preserve open periods and confirm other retention requirements before deleting original exports.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And Optional Entity Tax
paragraphs: Indiana generally subjects C corporations doing business in the state to adjusted gross income tax. Eligible partnerships, S corporations and similarly taxed LLCs may instead have a voluntary PTET election to evaluate for their owners. Preserve the actual classification and approved election. Neither a retail certificate nor the payroll withholding account establishes that the entity has made an income tax election.

Keep Indiana adjustments, receipt sourcing, owner allocation evidence and the federal return in the preparation file. Reconcile corporate or PTET estimates separately from state and county wage withholding; use the correct tax year and preserve any composite reporting support applicable to nonresident owners. At year end provide the election, owner changes, distributions, asset differences and payment confirmations. The preparer should reconcile owner credits with the entity calculation before statements are finalized.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: DWD requires covered employers to file quarterly unemployment wage reports and directs wages to the quarter in which they were paid. Contributory and reimbursable employers generally report electronically unless a waiver is granted. Keep employee wage detail, account notices and report acceptance with payment posting evidence. Reconcile contribution expense and unpaid liabilities monthly while preserving the original quarters of corrections. The annual payroll handoff should include those reports and the enhanced reporting fields announced for fourth quarter 2026.

sections.heading: A Fort Wayne Workshop Example

The bookkeeper retains the machinery invoice and delivery facts for use tax review, reconciles product sales before card fees, and keeps employee WH-4 certificates with state and county payroll totals. The preparer resolves the machinery treatment while payroll checks the county records.

sections.heading: Sales, Digital Products And Purchase Use Tax
paragraphs: Iowa Revenue explains that sales and use tax can apply to tangible goods, specified digital products and taxable services. The reporting file should describe what was sold and where delivery or first use occurred. Preserve gross sales, returns, tax collected and supported exclusions; do not presume every service or online subscription has the same treatment.

Iowa directs businesses to review purchases for tax the vendor did not collect. Keep the invoice, item or service description, use location, tax charged and review conclusion. Retain a workpaper connecting taxable purchases to the use tax portion of the return. Goods for resale, office equipment and purchased services should remain distinguishable in the vendor file.

sections.heading: Withholding And Unemployment Accounts
paragraphs: Revenue withholding uses periodic returns and payments based on the employer filing frequency. Its resources distinguish employee withholding certificates, tax payment records and wage statement reporting. Maintain payroll detail, account notices and filing confirmations so the amount withheld can be compared with actual remittances and statements.

Iowa Workforce Development operates myIowaUI separately from GovConnectIowa. Liable employers submit quarterly wage detail and employer payments electronically. Preserve employee wages by quarter, contribution calculations and account correspondence. Do not use the Revenue withholding account as a substitute for UI registration or assume a payroll debit proves that both agencies received reports.

sections.heading: Vendor Bills, Assets And Income Evidence
paragraphs: Recommended bookkeeping practice pairs vendor invoices with approval, delivery confirmation and payment. Retain credit memos and match them to purchases before settling supplier statements. If a repair business buys parts and equipment, separate resale stock from its own tools and document stock used internally. Keep asset purchase and disposal records for later basis review.

Record customer receipts against invoices and preserve the underlying gross amount when a processor deducts fees. Separate borrowing, owner funds and transfers from income. Keep customer contracts for deposits or extended projects and document refunds and bad debts. Expense descriptions should explain the business purpose rather than merely repeat a bank merchant name.
