sections.heading: Monthly Reporting And Tax Reconciliations
paragraphs: A practical monthly close reconciles banks and cards, merchant settlements, unpaid customer invoices, supplier balances and inventory. Prepare a profit and loss statement and balance sheet, with a cash forecast when large purchasing or payroll commitments are approaching. Review old suspense balances before relying on the reports.

Maintain separate tax movement schedules for sales/use, employee withholding and unemployment. Compare return totals to the ledger, payments to agency confirmations and closing balances to amounts still due. Preserve local sales detail where applicable. Explain any difference between the income statement, sales reporting and cash deposits through documented timing, fees or classification.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Year End And Retention Categories
paragraphs: Give the preparer annual reconciliations, sales and purchase tax workpapers, exemption support, payroll statements, myIowaUI reports, inventory counts, asset schedules and loan documents. Iowa requires wage statements containing Iowa withholding to be filed electronically through GovConnectIowa. Compare statement totals with periodic payroll and remittance records before filing.

Revenue says sales/use records such as bills, receipts, invoices and register documentation must be maintained for at least three years, and electronic records are permitted. It warns longer records can be requested when returns were never filed. Keep open audit periods and continuing asset records as appropriate; the sales/use minimum does not establish all employment or income tax retention requirements.

sections.heading: Business Income, Entity Elections And Owner Credits
paragraphs: Iowa has a corporation income tax program and an optional entity tax election for eligible partnerships and S corporations. The election applies for a single year and is binding once made for that year; a disregarded single member LLC cannot make its own election. Preserve federal and Iowa classifications, the approved election and owner schedules so entity payments and owners refundable credits can be traced.

Maintain Iowa income adjustments, source receipts and owner allocation evidence with the federal business return. Where estimates apply, Iowa directs the filing period to the final day of the tax year rather than the installment due date. Use that distinction in monthly payment reconciliations and keep entity estimates separate from payroll withholding. The annual handoff should include payment confirmations, credits, elections, ownership changes and any composite filing questions resolved by the preparer.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Iowa Workforce Development requires liable employers to submit quarterly wage detail and payment through myIowaUI. Its explanation distinguishes total wages and taxable wages used in the quarterly calculation and employer experience account. Retain the employee detail, contribution calculation and account notices. Reconcile employer unemployment expense and payable to posted payments each month, and preserve corrections at employee and quarter level. At year end compare the four quarterly files with payroll records and include unresolved notices separately from GovConnectIowa withholding confirmations.

sections.heading: A Cedar Rapids Service Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Cedar Rapids cleaning business serves a commercial building and a private home while buying supplies online. The bookkeeper keeps separate contracts and service locations, records gross customer receipts before card fees, and retains untaxed supply invoices for review. The preparer evaluates each service and purchase from those facts. Payroll withholding and myIowaUI contributions are reconciled separately.

sections.heading: Delivery Locations And Compensating Use Tax
paragraphs: Kansas Revenue generally sources delivered sales to the place the buyer receives the item. Preserve the actual delivery address and transaction details with sales records. The department publication separates gross sales, allowable deductions and tax collected; ordinary overhead does not become a sales tax deduction simply because it reduces operating profit.

Keep exemption certificates associated with the customer and transaction and preserve purchases used to calculate compensating use tax. For a vendor bill, identify what was bought, where it was delivered, whether it is stock or business equipment, and what tax was paid. Give uncertain treatment to the preparer. A supplier located outside Kansas does not establish the result by itself.

sections.heading: Withholding And Kansas Labor Records
paragraphs: Kansas withholding is deducted from the recipient and held for the state. Form KW-3 summarizes annual withholding deposits and transmits state wage or information statements. Retain employee certificates, pay registers, deposit reports and confirmations so the annual calculation can be traced to the actual withholding and payments.

Kansas Labor provides separate quarterly unemployment wage and contribution services and employer rate correspondence. Keep employee wage detail and the actual annual rate letter in that file. Agency text differs on electronic filing employee thresholds, so confirm the current requirement rather than using a threshold from an older FAQ. Report acceptance and payment posting should each be documented.

sections.heading: Vendor Payables And Operating Results
paragraphs: As general accounting practice, match supplier bills to approvals and goods received. Reconcile statements to open invoices and attach returns or credits. For equipment purchased with financing, preserve the original invoice, agreement and payment allocation. Record customer stock and property used by the business in separate categories so inventory and asset schedules remain understandable.

Maintain evidence for customer sales, deposits, refunds, loans and owner transactions. Processor settlements should reconcile gross customer activity, fees and cash received. Preserve business expense receipts and purpose even where the amount has no place as a sales tax deduction. This lets the income tax preparer and the owner evaluate the same transactions for different purposes.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Monthly Statements And Liability Schedules
paragraphs: Recommended monthly reports include a reconciled balance sheet, profit and loss statement, unpaid customer and supplier balances, and stock or project cost detail where useful. Reconcile bank, card and merchant accounts before interpreting sales trends. Identify stale invoices and duplicate supplier charges before paying them.

Roll sales tax, compensating use tax, withholding and unemployment balances forward by program. Compare gross sales and documented deductions to filed returns, then compare payments with agency activity. Keep jurisdiction allocations with the supporting transactions. A changing delivery pattern can change local reporting while the overall sales total remains similar.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Year End And Verified Retention
paragraphs: Prepare the annual handoff with reconciliations, local sales schedules, exemption evidence, purchase tax review, KW-3 support, unemployment filings, inventory counts, asset activity and financing balances. Explain refunds, prior period amendments and owner withdrawals. Preserve filing acknowledgments alongside the underlying calculation rather than only the payment receipt.

Kansas Publication KS-1510 says to keep sales tax records, including exemption certificates and tax exemption card copies, for the current business year and at least three prior years. This verified sales category should not be shortened to three years from an invoice date. Other payroll and income tax categories need separate retention review, and unresolved assessments require preservation.

sections.heading: Corporate And Partnership Income Records
paragraphs: Kansas imposes corporate income tax on corporations doing business in Kansas or deriving income from Kansas sources. Its partnership instructions separately require K-120S reporting for partnerships with Kansas source income or loss, regardless of amount. Preserve the federal classification and Kansas operations; an accounting loss or no customer payment in a month does not itself eliminate the annual information return.

Kansas partnership instructions call for the federal return, support for state modifications, credit schedules and an organization chart showing income flowing between entities. Keep those records with owner allocations and state source receipts. During monthly reconciliation, distinguish corporate estimates or other preparer directed entity payments from payroll and sales taxes. At year end provide the organization chart, ownership changes, state adjustments and payment history so the preparer can evaluate entity and owner reporting from the same supported balances.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Kansas Labor handles employer quarterly wage reports and unemployment contribution returns separately from Revenue withholding. The employer portal supplies the annual rate letter and calculates contribution information from reported wages. Retain employee wage detail and the actual rate correspondence, then reconcile employer expense and unpaid contributions to the accepted quarterly file and payment. Include corrections and account notices in the annual payroll handoff. Confirm current electronic filing requirements because the source page contains conflicting employee threshold statements.

sections.heading: A Wichita Delivery Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Wichita retailer delivers equipment to two Kansas customers in different local jurisdictions and buys display fixtures for its store. The bookkeeper retains exact delivery records, reconciles gross sales before processing fees and places the fixture invoices in the purchase tax review file. The preparer evaluates local sourcing and compensating use tax. Payroll records separately support KW-3 and Kansas Labor reporting.

sections.heading: Sales, Purchases And Exemption Support
paragraphs: Kentucky regulation 103 KAR 31:020 requires gross receipts, claimed deductions and purchase prices for relevant goods, digital property and services. Supporting evidence includes invoices, receipts, register records, bank statements, return workpapers and exemption data. Keep these documents connected to ledger entries so both taxed sales and exclusions can be explained.

For accounts payable, capture what was bought, whether it will be resold or used by the business, the Kentucky use location and tax charged. Preserve supplier credits and freight documents. Create a purchase review schedule for unclear tax treatment rather than inferring an exemption from a missing tax line. The preparer should determine service and digital property treatment from the contract and actual activity.

sections.heading: Employer Withholding And Unemployment
paragraphs: Kentucky Revenue directs employer withholding filing and payment to MyTaxes and provides wage statement reporting options. Keep employee certificates, payroll registers, tax deductions, payment confirmations and year end statement data together. Check the applicable filing period in the current account instructions; older paper form instructions should not control current electronic procedures.

Unemployment wage and tax reports use the separate Kentucky employer system. Preserve quarterly employee wages, account correspondence, contribution calculations and accepted report copies. Keep records of employee work locations for review of possible local employer obligations. State withholding does not establish that every local registration or worker classification question has been resolved.

sections.heading: Vendor Documentation And Income Evidence
paragraphs: General bookkeeping practice calls for purchase approval, a supplier bill, receiving evidence and payment allocation. Reconcile vendor statements before payment, retain disputed charges and credit memos, and document goods moved from stock into business use. Preserve equipment invoices and loan agreements so the asset and debt can be reviewed separately.

Connect customer receipts to invoices and contracts. Record gross sales before processing fees and keep advance payments distinct from borrowing and owner funding. Expense documentation should explain business purpose, especially when the bank description is vague or includes several items. Preserve inventory counts and asset disposal proceeds for the tax preparer.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Monthly Reconciliations And Management Reports
paragraphs: Recommended monthly reports include a profit and loss statement, balance sheet, receivable and payable aging, and inventory or project detail as appropriate. Reconcile cash, cards and processor clearing accounts, then review old reconciling items. Show upcoming payroll, supplier bills and tax payments in a cash forecast when timing is important.

Maintain distinct sales/use tax, employee withholding and unemployment schedules with opening balances, current accruals, payments and ending balances. Compare agency postings with submitted returns and explain prior period adjustments. Keep local liabilities separate when they actually apply, with their own notices and payment history.
sections.source_context: General bookkeeping reference. The example and monthly routine are practical illustrations, not additional state requirements.

sections.heading: Annual Handoff And Retention
paragraphs: Give the preparer annual reconciliations, sales and exemption schedules, purchase tax questions, payroll statements, unemployment filings, inventory records, asset transactions, financing balances and owner activity. Include accepted wage submissions and a list of amended periods. Identify unresolved local or employee location questions before the final annual package is closed.

KRS 139.720 requires relevant records for filers to be kept for at least four years from their creation unless Revenue authorizes earlier destruction in writing. The records regulation also ties preservation to the assessment limitation and extends preservation when the assessment period is extended. Apply both requirements; a four year anniversary alone does not establish permission to delete an open period.

sections.heading: Corporate Income And Limited Liability Entity Tax
paragraphs: Kentucky distinguishes corporation income tax from the Limited Liability Entity Tax, or LLET. Revenue describes LLET for businesses with liability protection, subject to statutory exclusions, while sole proprietorships and general partnerships do not fall into that same category. A federal disregarded entity classification alone does not settle Kentucky LLET treatment. Preserve formation, ownership and federal classification evidence for the preparer.

LLET uses Kentucky gross receipts or gross profits, with state restrictions on allowable cost of goods sold; it is not simply the income statement net profit. Maintain Kentucky and total receipts, returns, allowances and detailed production or merchandise costs. Reconcile corporation income and LLET estimates and credits separately from payroll during monthly review. At year end include the applicable calculations, state adjustments, owner information and payment confirmations so the preparer can evaluate liability and any interaction between the two taxes.

sections.heading: Unemployment Contributions And Wage Evidence
paragraphs: Kentucky unemployment reporting requires quarterly employee wage and tax files through its employer system, with separate access for authorized third party administrators. Preserve the employer number, wage detail, contribution notices and filed acknowledgments. Match employer unemployment expense and the payable to posted payments during the monthly close. Retain amendments with their original quarters and include the quarterly reconciliation and unresolved notices in the annual payroll package, independently of MyTaxes employee withholding.

sections.heading: A Lexington Mixed Purchase Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a Lexington business orders resale stock and office equipment on one supplier invoice, then receives a credit for damaged merchandise. The bookkeeper splits the purchase purposes, attaches the credit to the original bill and preserves Kentucky delivery information for tax review. Customer sales remain recorded before card fees. Payroll is reconciled independently between MyTaxes withholding and unemployment reports.
